In mathematics, '''Artin's criteria'''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Artin|first=M.|date=September 1974|title=Versal deformations and algebraic stacks|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=27|issue=3|pages=165–189|doi=10.1007/bf01390174|bibcode=1974InMat..27..165A |s2cid=122887093|issn=0020-9910}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Artin|first=M.|chapter=Algebraization of formal moduli: I|date=2015-12-31|title=Global Analysis: Papers in Honor of K. Kodaira (PMS-29)|pages=21–72|place=Princeton|publisher=Princeton University Press|doi=10.1515/9781400871230-003|isbn=978-1-4008-7123-0}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Artin|first=M.|date=January 1970|title=Algebraization of Formal Moduli: II. Existence of Modifications|journal=The Annals of Mathematics|volume=91|issue=1|pages=88–135|doi=10.2307/1970602|jstor=1970602|issn=0003-486X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Artin|first=M.|date=January 1969|title=Algebraic approximation of structures over complete local rings|journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|volume=36|issue=1|pages=23–58|doi=10.1007/bf02684596|s2cid=4617543|issn=0073-8301|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1969__36__23_0/}}</ref> are a collection of related [[necessary and sufficient condition]]s on deformation functors which prove the representability of these functors as either [[algebraic space]]s<ref name="HallRydh2013">{{cite journal|arxiv=1306.4599|first1=Jack|last1=Hall|first2=David|last2=Rydh|title=Artin's criteria for algebraicity revisited|journal=Algebra & Number Theory|year=2019|volume=13|issue=4|pages=749–796|doi=10.2140/ant.2019.13.749|s2cid=119597571}}</ref> or as [[algebraic stack]]s. In particular, these conditions are used in the construction of the [[moduli stack of elliptic curves]]<ref>{{Citation|last1=Deligne|first1=P.|author-link=Pierre Deligne|title=Modular Functions of One Variable II|pages=143–316|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-540-06558-6|last2=Rapoport|first2=M.|author-link2=Michael Rapoport|chapter=Les schémas de modules de courbes elliptiques |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|year=1973|volume=349|doi=10.1007/bfb0066716}}</ref> and the construction of the [[Moduli of algebraic curves|moduli stack of pointed curves]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Knudsen|first=Finn F.|date=1983-12-01|title=The projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves, II: The stacks $M_{g,n}$|url=https://www.mscand.dk/article/view/12001|journal=Mathematica Scandinavica|language=en|volume=52|pages=161–199|doi=10.7146/math.scand.a-12001|issn=1903-1807|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Notation and technical notes ==
Throughout this article, let <math>S</math> be a scheme of [[Finite type scheme|finite-type]] over a field <math>k</math> or an [[Excellent ring|excellent DVR]]. <math>p:F \to (Sch/S)</math> will be a [[category fibered in groupoids]], <math>F(X)</math> will be the groupoid lying over <math>X \to S</math>.

A stack <math>F</math> is called '''limit preserving''' if it is compatible with filtered direct limits in <math>Sch/S</math>, meaning given a filtered system <math>\{X_i\}_{i\in I}</math> there is an equivalence of categories<blockquote><math>\lim_{\rightarrow}F(X_i) \to F(\lim_{\rightarrow}X_i)</math></blockquote>An element of <math>x \in F(X)</math> is called an '''algebraic element''' if it is the [[henselization]] of an <math>\mathcal{O}_S</math>-algebra of finite type.

A limit preserving stack <math>F</math> over <math>Sch/S</math> is called an '''algebraic stack''' if

# For any pair of elements <math>x \in F(X), y \in F(Y)</math> the fiber product <math>X\times_F Y</math> is represented as an algebraic space
# There is a scheme <math>X \to S</math> locally of finite type, and an element <math>x \in F(X)</math> which is smooth and surjective such that for any <math>y \in F(Y)</math> the induced map <math>X\times_F Y \to Y</math> is smooth and surjective.
